messages.content: United moved our July 19 flight to Los Angeles more than two hours later. Can you compare leaving it alone with the earlier United connection and the other nonstop, including what each does to the car pickup and drive to Santa Monica?

The changed United nonstop now leaves ORD at 11:20 a.m. and reaches LAX at 1:49 p.m. Keeping it costs nothing. Avis is open until 11:30 p.m., so the counter will still be open, but a realistic pickup becomes about 2:45 p.m. That puts you on the road during heavier traffic and likely at Sea View around 4:00-4:45 p.m.

The earlier United option leaves at 6:05 a.m., connects in Denver for 58 minutes, and reaches LAX at 10:52 a.m. United will move all three tickets to it without a fare difference under the schedule-change waiver. A practical Avis pickup would be 11:45 a.m., with arrival in Santa Monica around 12:45-1:30 p.m. Its drawback is the connection: the first leg needs to run close to schedule, and a missed connection could erase the time advantage.

The comparable American nonstop leaves ORD at 8:40 a.m. and arrives at 11:12 a.m. Rebooking three travelers after refunding United would add $342 total. Avis pickup would be about 12:05 p.m., and Sea View arrival around 1:00-1:45 p.m.
How reliable is that Denver connection versus just paying for American?

American is the cleanest operational choice because it avoids a connection and arrives only 20 minutes after the earlier United itinerary. Its main cost is the additional $342, and changing carriers would separate the outbound from United confirmation N4K8TZ while leaving the Monday SAN-ORD return on United.

The Denver itinerary has enough connection time for a normal same-terminal transfer, and United protects the onward segment if the first flight is late. Based on the current schedule, there are two later United DEN-LAX flights that day, so the recovery options are reasonable. Still, a delay of roughly 30 minutes or more leaving Chicago could make the planned connection tight.

Keeping the shifted nonstop has the lowest disruption risk after departure, but it gives up nearly three hours in Los Angeles and moves most of the airport-to-coast drive into afternoon traffic.
Put total trip cost and likely first-night timing side by side.

Keeping the shifted United nonstop leaves the confirmed trip total at $5,613. Expected car pickup is 2:45 p.m.; Sea View check-in is likely 4:00-4:45 p.m.

Taking the earlier United connection also leaves the total at $5,613. Expected pickup is 11:45 a.m.; you should reach Santa Monica around 12:45-1:30 p.m., though the room may not yet be ready. A missed Denver connection could instead push arrival into the afternoon or evening.

Taking the American nonstop raises the trip total to $5,955. Expected pickup is 12:05 p.m.; Sea View arrival is likely 1:00-1:45 p.m.

All three preserve Sea View July 19-22, the July 22 drive south, Bahia Mission Bay July 22-27, the one-way Avis return at SAN, and the United flight home Monday, July 27 at 11:35 a.m.
Is the Avis counter actually okay with us showing up later if we keep the changed flight? I don't want the reservation released.

Avis will hold this prepaid-time-window reservation for up to two hours after the scheduled 12:45 p.m. pickup when the flight number is attached. The changed nonstop's expected 2:45 p.m. collection lands at that limit, so even a modest baggage or traffic delay inside LAX could require a call to keep it active. The counter remains open, but the hold window is the concern.

For either earlier alternative, I can revise the pickup time without changing the $684 pay-later total or the July 27 SAN return.
For this trip, I'm willing to take the connection. The $342 isn't worth it when United has later Denver flights as backup. Move us to the early United option.

Before I submit it: change all three outbound tickets to United ORD-DEN-LAX on July 19, departing 6:05 a.m. and arriving 10:52 a.m., with no fare difference. Keep the July 27 SAN-ORD flight, both hotels, and the one-way Avis reservation unchanged apart from moving LAX pickup earlier. Correct?
Correct. Set the car pickup for 11:45.
The airline change is permitted under the schedule-change waiver, and the Avis time adjustment remains at the same rate. I’ll complete both now.

Completed. United confirmation N4K8TZ now has Marcus, Daniel, and Owen departing ORD July 19 at 6:05 a.m., connecting in Denver for 58 minutes, and arriving at LAX at 10:52 a.m. There was no fare difference. The Monday, July 27 SAN-ORD flight remains unchanged at 11:35 a.m.-5:42 p.m.

Avis confirmation AVD-904671 now shows LAX pickup at 11:45 a.m. on July 19. The SAN return remains July 27 at 9:30 a.m., and the pay-later total remains $684. Sea View Santa Monica remains confirmed July 19-22 and Bahia Mission Bay July 22-27. The full confirmed trip total is still $5,613. With an on-time arrival, expect to reach the rental counter around 11:35-11:50 a.m. and Santa Monica around 12:45-1:30 p.m.
